fixes.explanation: Yes, baker! Acts 1:13 says they went to the upper room where they were staying. They came back to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives (Acts 1:12) and went to a room with a little altitude. I respect any room that comes with altitude.

Simon the tanner is a real man in Acts, but he's in a different spot. Peter stays with him in Joppa, a coastal town (Acts 9:43). In this passage, the apostles go to an upper room in Jerusalem. Different city, different host, but nice memory for names, friend.

Prayer is the word. Acts 1:14 says, “With one accord they all continued in prayer…” Notice the words "With one accord…" They're all stirring the same bowl in the same direction. And they keep at it. They continue.

Lazarus, Mary and Martha are a real family. Jesus raised Lazarus from the dead (John 11:43-44). But Acts 1:14 doesn't list them here. It names Mary the mother of Jesus and His brothers, along with the women. Good guess, friend, those are names worth remembering.

Nicodemus and Joseph of Arimathea take care of Jesus's body after the cross (John 19:38-39). Acts 1:14 doesn't put them here, though. The verse names Mary the mother of Jesus and His brothers. Good guess, friend, those are names worth remembering.

Right on. Acts 1:15 says it was “a gathering of about a hundred and twenty…” That's a lot of people standing around while Peter stands up. And notice it says "about," so I won't claim it's an exact headcount.
Seventy is a nice round number, but it's not the one in this verse. Acts 1:15 says the gathering was about a hundred and twenty. I'd have needed a few extra trays for that many people.

Blood is right. Acts 1:19 says the people in Jerusalem called the field Akeldama in their own language, that is, Field of Blood. I think this part of the story is heavy. We'll let it be heavy and move on gently.

Silver is a fair guess, since the verse before talks about a reward. Acts 1:18 says Judas bought a field with the reward for his wickedness, but it doesn't name the reward. The name of the field, Akeldama, means Field of Blood (Acts 1:19). I think this verse hurts a little, and it's okay to feel that.

They pray, yes. Acts 1:24 says, “And they prayed…” and then they ask the Lord to show them which of the two He has chosen. Two names are on the table, and they take it to the Lord. I do the same before I open the oven.

Calling in the elders sounds sensible, friend. I'd probably schedule a meeting about the meeting. But the text doesn't mention any elders being sent for. After they propose the two men, Acts 1:24 says they prayed.

Letting each man speak sounds fair, and I'd probably want a speech or two myself. But the passage never says either man spoke. What it does say is that they prayed (Acts 1:24). Prayer is what's on the page, so that's where I'm staying, baker.
Heart is the word. They pray, “Lord, You know everyone’s heart. Show us which of these two You have chosen…” (Acts 1:24) They ask the One who knows hearts to show them. That's the whole request.
Past is a fair guess, friend. But their prayer says, “Lord, You know everyone’s heart.” (Acts 1:24) They name the heart, not the past. It's a small difference, but it's the one the text uses.

Silas didn't make the list, friend. The text gives two names: Joseph called Barsabbas, also known as Justus, and Matthias (Acts 1:23). The lot fell to Matthias (Acts 1:26). Silas can't win a lot he was never put into.
